result.scientific_strategy:
## 9f0c1a9e-23c2-4c48-85a6-09cb6d902999 / Scientific strategy

**Direction:** Retain the experiment-2 full-radius working lineage as the strongest measured recipe. Unchanged continuation did not improve it, experiment 5's explicit inverse-kinematic joint-limit margins produced a severe broad regression, experiment 6's measured negative-angle oversampling did not repair the recurring failures, and experiment 7's higher action-effort penalty did not improve them. The next useful investigation should target observation-contract behavior or a more targeted control diagnostic while preserving the official task distribution; the tested angular oversampling and action-cost changes should not be repeated unchanged.

**Lessons and limits:** Experiment 2's full-radius transfer produced 197/200 (98.5%) on the fixed task-reference panel at checkpoints 100352 and 120832, versus 196/200 (98.0%) for the selected baseline. At checkpoint 100352, sub-14 cm success improved from 101/105 to 103/105, while above-14 cm success fell from 95/95 to 94/95; the distinct 200-episode research panel tied the baseline at 98.5% with zero discordant outcomes. This partially supports broader radius coverage for particular small-radius cases, but not a robust gain or a causal claim. Experiment 3 trained the proposed negative-angle bias for 120,832 steps and produced 24 checkpoints, but none had a task-reference or research-evaluation artifact; its proxy and reward trajectory were training diagnostics only, so its hypothesis was inconclusive. Experiment 4 measured three continued checkpoints on the same development panels: task-reference success was 98.5% (20480), 95.0% (95232), and 97.5% (120832), while research-evaluation success was 98.0%, 97.0%, and 96.5%. The best continuation tied, rather than exceeded, the parent's 98.5% task-reference result, and the training proxy did not track later task regressions. This weakens the insufficient-training explanation on that trajectory, but one continuation from one parent and one seed cannot prove a general PPO plateau or identify a causal mechanism. Experiment 5's 13-value observation with branch-level joint-limit margins collapsed broadly: both measured task-reference checkpoints achieved 23/200 (11.5%), versus 197/200 for working, and research-panel success was 22/200 (11.0%) and 19/200 (9.5%). Its paired comparisons had no candidate wins, so the tested intervention was deprioritized; fresh initialization and one seed prevent attributing the collapse to feature semantics alone. Experiment 6 then measured the angular-coverage hypothesis directly. On the fixed task-reference panel, checkpoint-100352 scored 193/200 (96.5%) and checkpoint-105472 scored 195/200 (97.5%), versus 197/200 (98.5%) for working. The recurring failures at seeds 7384 and 7402 and the high-radius failure at seed 7475 persisted at both checkpoints. The candidate had no paired wins and lost four episodes at 100352 and two at 105472; at 100352 its negative-sub-14 cm group was 52/57 versus 55/57 for working and its positive-sub-14 cm group was 47/48 versus 48/48, while the other radius/angle groups tied. On the research panel, the candidates scored 196/200 (98.0%) and 195/200 (97.5%), below working's 197/200 (98.5%), with one and two paired losses respectively and no wins. Training diagnostics were non-monotonic: proxy success was 0.974 at 5120, fell to 0.85 at 41984, reached 0.99 at 105472, and ended at 0.94; reward peaked at 121.9 around 60416 and ended at 99.9. These results contradict the expected measured improvement under the tested transfer run and show that this angular sampling recipe did not resolve the failure cluster. Experiment 7 increased ACTION_COST_COEFFICIENT from 0.01 to 0.05 while preserving the full-radius recipe and policy I/O. Task-reference success was 196/200 (98.0%) at 100352, 195/200 (97.5%) at 110592, and 196/200 (98.0%) at 120832; none exceeded the parent's 197/200 (98.5%). The recurring failures at seeds 7384 and 7402 and the high-radius seed 7475 persisted at every measured checkpoint; seed 7300 also failed at all three, and seed 7310 failed at 110592. Research-panel success was 197/200 (98.5%), 196/200 (98.0%), and 196/200 (98.0%); the first checkpoint had no discordant paired outcomes, while later checkpoints each lost one episode to working and had no candidate wins. The first research-panel score is a partial positive signal, but it did not transfer to task-reference improvement or recover the recurring cases. The tested action-effort change therefore provides measured evidence against this recipe, not proof that all control costs or action limits are causal. Its training proxy and reward also remained diagnostics rather than task-performance evidence. Across experiments 5-7, one seed per changed recipe, repeated development panels, and no official benchmark limit causal and generalization claims.

**Open questions:** Are the recurring failures near 9-10 cm and -123 to -128 degrees caused primarily by policy I/O or normalization behavior, a more specific control limitation, or another representation issue rather than target coverage or this action-cost weight? How much of checkpoint variation persists under another seed or distinct panel? Can a targeted intervention improve those cases without creating positive-angle or high-radius regressions, and can any candidate exceed 98% across more than one development panel before official assessment? The experiment-5 collapse remains unresolved at the component level because feature semantics, scaling, initialization, and optimization were not separated.

**Conditional next steps:** Restore the experiment-2 working lineage and complete recipe; this is a measured practical choice, not proof that every fresh augmented run would fail. Do not reuse the experiment-5 joint-limit-margin, experiment-6 negative-angle-oversampling, or experiment-7 action-cost interventions unchanged. Prefer an observation-contract diagnostic with feature scaling and normalization explicit, or a narrowly instrumented control investigation that measures the recurring geometry directly. Retain a direction only if task measurements improve the recurring cases without positive- or high-radius tradeoffs on a distinct panel; broad regression, a neutral paired result, or training-only improvement should deprioritize it. Do not request the official benchmark until development evidence is stronger than the current threshold-level result.
